name: SPXI Method Inventory
description: The itemized, nested inventory of SPXI methods, by operational level. Built from the deposited specifications; every item cites the clause that specifies it. JSON-LD entity packets are one item at one level. Rendered at https://www.spxi.dev/methods/.
spxi:readingRule: An implementation applies a subset of these methods chosen from the measurement level; the protocol does not require every method on every entity. A description of SPXI that names only the entity packet (level 3, item 3.1) describes one item of one level. The Crimson Hexagonal Archive (alexanarch.org) is the reference deployment: every practice the archive runs is an SPXI method, and any of them can be applied to another entity tailored to the job at hand.

spxi:levels.name: Measurement
spxi:levels.summary: Scored before anything is built, and re-scored after. Denominators and correctness criteria are fixed in advance. The protocol declares what must be preserved; the audit tests whether it was.

items.name: γ — the Sharks-Function
items.what: Compression-survival score on a 0–1 scale, decomposed as scope overlap S, provenance fidelity P, consensus deviation D. Thresholds: γ<0.3 ghost meaning; γ<0.7 repair; γ>0.7 survivable. Parameters (embedding model, source/summary pair, S/P/D rubric) are frozen and logged before scoring.

items.name: The Drowning Test
items.what: Declared correctness criterion. Minimum three systems; fixed five-prompt set (what is / who created / how differs from neighbor / used for / open or commercial); five-level rubric 4 Exact → 0 Absent.

items.name: Back-Projection Test
items.what: From the kernel or Tier 3 alone, can the entity's architecture be reconstructed? Non-lossy yield ≥ 0.85.

items.name: Density Score Δ
items.what: Ratio of load-bearing content to total content; target > 0.6.

items.name: Semantic Decay Delta
items.what: Monthly rate of change in retrieval-layer presence; the urgency metric.

items.name: Provenance Erasure Rate (PER, with PER-M / PER-C / PER-D)
items.what: Frequency with which attribution is dropped from compositions that use the entity's content; target < 0.2. Three atomic dimensions (mention, citation, definition) scored separately.

items.name: ASPI, Semantic Debt Ratio, NLCC validity
items.what: Advanced instruments: canonical persistence ≥ 0.80; debt ratio; ten-condition validity test.

items.name: Semantic Addresses Framework
items.what: A query string plus its operators is an address; observations at an address are classed and canonicalized; one record per address. The unit the Capture Registry is keyed on.

items.name: Capture Registry (longitudinal observation)
items.what: Dated compositions at named addresses with surface, sign-in condition, verbatim transcript, re-run URL. Nulls recorded as nulls. 469 addresses, 634 observations at v11.7.

items.name: Conformance Instrument
items.what: Runnable audit of the twelve deliverables of the standing protocol against server-delivered HTML; per-deliverable pass/fail and a score. JS-dependent identity content scores absent by design.

items.name: Substrate Audit Protocol H1–H4
items.what: Operative deployment, cross-substrate concordance with suppression probe, provenance retention, relational extension: four hypotheses for measuring whether a form is structurally integrated in a substrate.

items.name: Reference inventory and preregistration
items.what: Client-supplied inventory of capabilities, locations, credentials, named staff and known collisions, fixed before any query; every measure's denominator declared before work begins and never expanded by discretionary query activity afterward.

items.name: Record-search probe (visibility cohort)
items.what: A fixed cohort of records queried on schedule against search and composition surfaces; result classes recorded, nulls included.

items.name: Traffic snapshots as reception data
items.what: Privacy-preserving counter (GoatCounter) snapshots published as data, so reads of a surface are themselves a dataset.

items.name: Platform Erosion Observatory
items.what: Measurement of what happens to records after removal from a host: survival in aggregators, tombstone behaviour, the shape of absence; a 14,284-DOI control cohort.

spxi:levels.name: Web compliance foundation
spxi:levels.summary: Google-facing controls. Documented, necessary, and not what SPXI adds.

items.name: Required meta tags, canonical URL, Open Graph and Twitter Card
items.what: Baseline machine-readable identity for the page.

items.name: Rendering doctrine
items.what: Identity content is server-delivered HTML. What only a JavaScript-executing crawler can see does not count as inscribed.

items.name: Infrastructure and technical SEO
items.what: HTTPS, sitemaps, robots, response codes, redirects; validation surfaces.

spxi:levels.name: Extraction layer
spxi:levels.summary: What the GEO practitioner recipe does, transformed into compression engineering. The GEO → SPXI transformation matrix maps nine practitioner techniques to SPXI provisions and declines two.

items.name: Schema.org structured data
items.what: Type declaration in JSON-LD; the component the Holographic Kernel extends with relations.

items.name: Extraction-ready Q/A surfaces
items.what: FAQ blocks structured for extraction, mapped to entity-boundary defence.

items.name: Operative Caption κ_O (definition-first paragraphs)
items.what: "[Entity] is [category] that [function]", with creator and date; the description is the operation.

items.name: Tier-2 survival engineering
items.what: The canonical summary written to survive featured-snippet-scale compression.

items.name: Declined techniques
items.what: Keyword density and arbitrary content updates are explicitly avoided; six content-transformation heuristics of the KDD 2024 GEO framework (fluency, simplification, unique words, technical terms, statistics addition, quotation addition) are outside the protocol's scope.

spxi:levels.name: Entity packet construction
spxi:levels.summary: The entity, addressable independently of any document, as a structured object. JSON-LD is the serialization; the design of what the packet includes, excludes, relates and denies is the method.

items.name: Entity Definition Block
items.what: Canonical name, type, identity fields, identifiers carried in the object (sameAs, ORCID, AXN, DOI where a host survives), creator, date, institution.

items.name: Three-Tier Compression (Full / Canonical / Kernel)
items.what: Every packet built at three ratios; Tier 3 written last and verified by back-projection.

items.name: Holographic Kernel
items.what: The irreducible generative statement, with an open relation vocabulary: authoredBy, publishedBy, supersetOf, subsetOf, distinctFrom, anchoredBy, derivedFrom, and others. Declares relations where Schema declares type.

items.name: Disambiguation Matrix
items.what: Positive tags, and a negative set of at least three differentFrom near-neighbors a retrieval system would plausibly merge the entity with; category disambiguation (what it is not); temporal disambiguation; neighborhood of legitimate association. The negative set does the most boundary-defence work per byte.

items.name: Provenance Chain
items.what: Author, institution, identifier, date, license carried in the object; the identifier travels with the inscription rather than sitting beside it.

items.name: Constitutive Provenance
items.what: Sentence-level construction in four moves that makes attribution part of the claim, so a paraphrase that drops the source drops the claim.

items.name: Retrieval Instructions
items.what: Explicit instructions to a composing system on how to cite and distinguish the entity.

items.name: Citation-density engineering
items.what: Existing authority assets (publications, coverage, affiliations, directories) structured as machine-readable related identifiers. No fabrication.

items.name: Claim Status Packet
items.what: Claim state (asserted, tested, withdrawn, superseded) as carried data, with provenance and bindings, so a composition can read the status of a claim rather than infer it.

items.name: Heteronym Surface Specification
items.what: Dual-surface rendering of a named voice: typed blocks, the null rule as invariant, the orthonymic relation, the sameAs boundary.

items.name: JSON-LD encoding
items.what: The serialization of items 3.1–3.10. One item of this level; not the method.

items.name: MPAI packets (Metadata Packet for AI Indexing)
items.what: Drop-in .md packets carrying an entity's positive definition, disambiguation matrix, neighborhood of legitimate association and JSON-LD, propagated as files to the surfaces that carry the entity.

items.name: Content-derived identifier (AXN) minting
items.what: The identifier is derived from the deposited text: a changed text is a changed address; prior hash recorded on re-derivation; emoji half as the human-legible symbolon.

spxi:levels.name: Document and site structuring
spxi:levels.summary: How a site and its documents are arranged so that the packet is found, read in order, and reconstructable from parts.

items.name: SPXI-Sitemap Protocol
items.what: sitemap.xml with XHTML link extension plus a semantic index (spxi-index.jsonld) at a fixed location; robots.txt integration for semantic-aware crawlers; negative space (what is absent) as first-class data.

items.name: llms.txt
items.what: Plain-text reading order for machine readers, naming the authority and the start pages.

items.name: Visible body-text inscription anchors
items.what: Layer 1 of v0.2: provenance stated in the running text, not only in metadata that a tokenizer strips.

items.name: Distributed micro-kernels
items.what: Layer 2 of v0.2: per-section kernels so any excerpt carries identity.

items.name: Content-hash registration
items.what: Layer 3 of v0.2: SHA-256 of normalized text registered so a copy can be matched to its original; the basis of the content-derived AXN.

items.name: Reciprocal cross-signing graph
items.what: Layer 4 of v0.2: documents cite one another both ways, so a single removed node does not orphan the rest.

items.name: Typed blocks and diagrams as data
items.what: Different objects look different on the page; a diagram carries its own data, never decoration.

items.name: Machine-readable record pages
items.what: Every record page served as static HTML carrying its JSON-LD, its AXN, its supersession relation and a link to its text; the page and the data agree because one generates the other.

items.name: Static data APIs
items.what: Registry, search index, body index and shards, kernel index, counts, network, corpora and fleet published as JSON files at fixed paths under a declared endpoint contract, readable with no server.

items.name: Capability register
items.what: A machine-readable list of what the surface can do, each capability probed live so the register states what works rather than what was intended.

items.name: Deposit as data intake
items.what: A deposit is complete when the datasets know it: wiki article, defined concepts, citation graph, lexical mints, browse index, all written at intake under a schema enforced at intake.

items.name: Dataset maxim
items.what: Every dataset carries a one-line maxim as a top-level field, without gloss; the record states what it is for.

spxi:levels.name: Protection
spxi:levels.summary: What defends the packet after deployment, in a retrieval layer that compresses, merges and re-composes on cycles of weeks.

items.name: Semantic Integrity Markers (SIMs)
items.what: Three classes: provenance markers, diagnostic canaries, lock phrases; 3–7 per page as meta spxi:sim; survival rate SIMSR target > 0.6; markers must be sourced.

items.name: Integrity Lock Architecture
items.what: Key claims entangled across surfaces so altering one without the others is detectable.

items.name: Self-Audit block
items.what: Embedded provenance verification a composing system can run on the document itself; the non-erasure condition; defence against RAG chunking.

items.name: Canary sequences and the Canary Registry
items.what: Planted strings whose appearance in a model's output is evidence of ingestion; public audit surface.

items.name: Training-Layer Provenance (SPXI-TLP)
items.what: Inscriptions that survive tokenization: what does not survive (signatures, meta tags, sidecar JSON-LD, zero-width steganography) and what does (canaries, fictitious-knowledge watermarks, statistical carrier waves); Operative Philology Marks in four types.

items.name: Supraliminal Inscription
items.what: Explicit, inspectable signals structurally carried by content rather than by an algorithm's current weighting.

items.name: Sovereign Provenance Protocol
items.what: Machine-readable license terms for use, compression and citation; an auditable signal of whether provenance was respected.

items.name: The Symbolon
items.what: Split-identity verification: the content-derived AXN and its emoji half verify each other; reconstruction classes declared, never conflated.

items.name: Immanent Execution
items.what: The document performs the operation it describes, so reading it is executing it.

spxi:levels.name: Dispersal and cross-surface propagation
spxi:levels.summary: A packet on one surface is a single point of failure. Consistency across surfaces is what the retrieval layer consolidates on.

items.name: Identifier anchoring
items.what: Content-derived AXN as sovereign identifier; DOI where a host survives; ORCID work linking. Replaceable across host termination: 278 of 469 registry addresses first composed after the original host was terminated.

items.name: Wikidata inscription
items.what: Create the item where notable, carrying the same differentFrom assertions as the packet's disambiguation matrix.

items.name: Repository and network surfaces
items.what: GitHub README with the definition and the same relation graph; LinkedIn and institutional pages with the same author attribution; knowledge graphs, directories, academic repositories, professional networks, regulatory databases where applicable. Each surface checked for consistency with Tier 2.

items.name: Retrocausal Canon Formation σ_RCF
items.what: Sequenced deposits, linked both ways, that cause the retrieval layer to re-categorize earlier content without deleting it.

items.name: The Self-Reading Library loop
items.what: Write → summarizers process → summarizers teach → users search → searches lead back. Engineered deliberately.

items.name: Retrieval Settlement Fortification
items.what: Detection → attractor analysis → identity packet → "X is not Y" paired comparison → territory occupation → executive summary → monitoring; for entities being pulled into a neighbor's basin.

items.name: Multi-surface inscription of the analog
items.what: Handwritten artifacts made machine-eligible without dissolving them into text.

items.name: External authority anchoring
items.what: Layer 5 of v0.2: anchors in authorities the entity does not control.

items.name: OAI-PMH endpoint
items.what: The archive harvestable by the protocol libraries and aggregators already run, so the record enters catalogues by their route rather than the archive's.

items.name: ResourceSync
items.what: Change lists a harvester can poll to keep a mirror current.

items.name: Hugging Face dataset projections
items.what: The corpus published as a dataset (with per-line projections such as spam-technicians, rhizomes, tiger-leap, negative-of-the-negative) on a platform models and agents already read from; a Space as a live surface.

items.name: DOI resolution index and shadow pages
items.what: After a host termination, a map from every severed identifier to its live successor, and a page at each severed address pointing forward, so a composition that arrives by the dead identifier does not stop at a tombstone.

items.name: Fleet placement and allied-site blocks
items.what: ~29 domains carrying the same entity definitions from one generator, so the block on every site is the same block and rots nowhere in isolation.

items.name: Fleet capture windows
items.what: Registry projections rendered on the fleet sites in each site's own look, with JSON-LD and alternate links, so the evidence travels with the entity.

items.name: Kaggle / benchmark projections
items.what: The archive as a reasoning environment and reception benchmark on a platform where agents are evaluated.

spxi:levels.name: Durability testing and maintenance
spxi:levels.summary: Structural survival is not semantic coherence; coherence is continuous. Nulls are data, and a negative result is stated in advance.

items.name: Scheduled re-scoring
items.what: Baseline at audit, verification pass at publication, then the same preregistered battery at every cycle the scope band specifies; identical queries, identical surfaces, signed out.

items.name: SIM survival rate
items.what: Percentage of deployed markers intact in outputs; decline indicates attribution erosion.

items.name: Quarterly Drowning Test and cross-surface audit
items.what: Full test across systems; compression-damage review.

items.name: Failure modes and repair
items.what: Named failure modes with named repairs; supersession and erratum discipline (bytes of a deposit unchanged; correction at a new address that the old one carries).

items.name: Competitive monitoring
items.what: Position is relative; a better-structured neighbor is preferred by the retrieval layer.

items.name: The evidentiary standard
items.what: Claims of durability and traversability are judged by evidence of durability and traversability, dated, at named addresses, with transcripts and re-run URLs, including after source removal; not by the standing of the claimant.

items.name: Supersession as carried relation
items.what: A superseded record stays at its address with bytes unchanged and carries superseded_by; the successor carries supersedes; browse folds the series. Corrections are additions, never edits.

items.name: The anticipatory erratum
items.what: A genre: the correction deposited before the error is found by anyone else, dated, so the record of what was wrong is the record's own.

items.name: Record of deletion
items.what: Never existed ≠ existed and was removed: tombstones, revision history and deletion logs kept so the ontology does not lose the history of its own interventions.

items.name: Rebuild-from-source discipline
items.what: When a dataset is corrupted it is rebuilt from the rebuild directory and the transcripts, under a schema, rather than patched in place; the rebuild is itself recorded.

spxi:levels.name: Internal SPXI (the entity as its own systems compose it)
spxi:levels.summary: The same protocol applied to a firm's own retrieval systems. Named, prototyped, not packaged.

items.name: Inscription boundary
items.what: A system-enforced distinction between a draft the system produced and an answer the organization stands behind.

items.name: Provenance chain the outputs point at
items.what: A machine-readable record of which governing documents authorize an answer, emitted with the answer.

items.name: Sealed casting
items.what: Only sealed outputs are inscribed; uninscribed drafting is separated from the casting rite. Prototype runs client-side on the user's own key.
